title: Composition of pro-etale module inverse images with canonical constant coefficients
statement:
Let $g:Z\to X$ and $f:X\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites and universe conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with constant ring sheaves $\Lambda_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h=f,g,f\circ g$ let $h^*$ and $h_*$ be the module inverse image and direct image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], using precisely its canonical constant-section map $c^h_\Lambda$. There is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$(f\circ g)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*f^*:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_Z).$$
It is the canonical comparison of left adjoints to the direct-image identification $(f\circ g)_*\cong f_*g_*$ induced on each object $V\to Y$ by $Z\times_X(X\times_YV)\cong Z\times_YV$, with the module actions given by the specified constant-section maps.

proof.text: For the independent coefficient universe, use the canonical base-change pasting isomorphism MorphismProperty.Over.pullbackComp of [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Mathlib Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' gives the commutative-ring direct-image comparison. Its component is restriction along the pasting isomorphism, natural both in site objects and in sheaves.

proof.text: For each scheme morphism, the hom-equivalence of the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] shows that the constant-presheaf unit followed by the prescribed coefficientProEtaleDirectRingMap of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is the target constant-presheaf unit at the base-changed object. Apply injectivity of this hom-equivalence to the two candidate coefficient maps for a composite. On each object, the two unit identities and naturality of toSheafify [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] identify their components. Hence rho for the composite equals the iterated rho followed by the pasting comparison, in arbitrary independent coefficient universe.

proof.text: Forget the commutative coefficient rings to rings and apply the equality of step 2 componentwise. Use Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp, pushforwardNatIso along the canonical pasting isomorphism, and pushforwardCongr along this equality to obtain d from the iterated module direct image to the composite direct image. These constructions on [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] act respectively as the identity, restriction along pasting, and identity on sections. Thus d has precisely the section formula in the Lean statement.

proof.text: Let e be conjugateIsoEquiv of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] for the composite adjunction and the single adjunction, in the order of the Lean statement. Take a=e.symm d. The identity e(a)=d follows by apply_symm_apply. Any other a' satisfying the predicate has mate d' with the same prescribed section formula. Extensionality of natural transformations, module-sheaf morphisms, and sectionwise linear maps gives d'=d. Injectivity of e then gives a'=a, proving unique existence.
